# TERMs with `line` `formal-apparatus`

*Lines of inquiry — A named line of the record's own argument, so that a line can be set aside as a whole and what depends on it can be found. Retracting a line is a status change on its members, never a deletion (ADR-032).*

**Formal apparatus** — results that hold whatever any substantive line concludes — gluing and contextuality, comparison of experiments and probes, identifiability, conservation, and thresholds for naming a unit; held as a second line by the general results other lines borrow, so that setting a substantive line aside does not retire them (ADR-040).

| [TERM-140](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-140.md) v4 | sloppy | At the owner's suggestion of 2026-11-21, after the filing of the exchange "Rich Get Richer Power Laws": "a TERM for the mathematical (information geometric?) sense of 'sloppy' might be merited". A model is sloppy, at a parameter point and for a given observation design, when the eigenvalues of its Fisher information, in a declared chart (conventionally the logarithms of its bare parameters), spread evenly over many decades, no gap among them marks off the combinations that matter from those that do not, and the eigenvectors are skewed from the bare parameter axes. The term separates this from three neighbours: ill-conditioning (one ratio, which a single gap can produce), singularity (a zero eigenvalue on a stratum), and the hyperribbon (the chart-free shape of the predictions, [TERM-135](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-135.md)). It says nothing of the law by which the spectrum falls. Its job is to let the record's entries on sloppiness, singular learning and effective dimension say which of these they mean. The source of the concept is Sethna and colleagues: LIT-2977, LIT-3009 and LIT-2994, read on 2026-11-21 (THEORY-2156, THEORY-2155, THEORY-2154), and the survey LIT-2999, read the same day (THEORY-2165). The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
